svg.text: Patterns you already own — Uber reuses your Top-K + Ticketmaster muscles
same components, different trigger — one new idea per system (see /system-design/top-k and /system-design/ticketmaster)
Smooth the write path — SAME as Top-K
Top-K: Kafka absorbs 700k views/s → Flink pre-aggregates
Uber: location pings 600k/s → throttled + batched + DYNAMIC
updates (status/speed/proximity-aware) cut it to ~100k/s
rule: don't let every event hit the expensive store
Consistency via TTL lock — SAME as Ticketmaster
TM: ticket lock SET NX TTL 10 min → one buyer per seat
Uber: driver lock SET driverId TTL 5 s → one request per driver
rule: TTL auto-release beats cron cleanup every time
Queue-as-admission-control — SAME as Ticketmaster
TM: virtual waiting queue absorbs onsale stampede
Uber: ride-request queue (partitioned by region) absorbs
stadium/NYE surge; matcher crash = re-delivery, not loss
rule: queue ≠ storage here — it's admission control
The ONE new idea in Uber
2D geospatial indexing — genuinely new:
· quadtree (PostGIS): density-aware, rebalance cost
· geohash (Redis): fixed precision, write-friendly
uneven density → quadtree · high-frequency writes → geohash
Interview one-liner when asked "why another system instead of my old patterns?":
every one of these is a NEW TRIGGER on a pattern you know — the novelty Uber adds is WHERE + HOW FAST (2D space, seconds, 3M devices).
